title: A discrete generative model of neuronal spiking activity on microelectrode arrays
abstract: arXiv:2609.23907v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Generative models of neural activity could help characterize tissue dynamics, compare experimental conditions, and simulate population activity for applications ranging from disease and drug-response studies to closed-loop experimentation. Existing approaches, however, typically assume a fixed set of sorted neurons, whereas high-density microelectrode arrays produce extremely sparse, array-wide binary spike volumes in which the observed subset of electrodes varies across assays. We introduce a discrete generative model that represents this activity using a shared vocabulary of spatiotemporal motifs. A residual vector-quantized autoencoder learns the motif vocabulary, while a factorized masked transformer predicts where activity occurs and which motif appears at each active location. translated_title: 微电极阵列上神经元尖峰活动的离散生成模型
translated_abstract: 神经活动的生成模型可以帮助表征组织动力学、比较实验条件以及模拟群体活动，其应用范围涵盖疾病与药物反应研究到闭环实验。然而，现有方法通常假设一组固定的已分选神经元，而高密度微电极阵列产生的是极其稀疏的、覆盖整个阵列的二值尖峰体数据，其中观测到的电极子集在不同实验之间各不相同。我们提出了一种离散生成模型，利用共享的时空模式词表来表示这种活动。残差向量量化自编码器学习模式词表，而分解式掩码变换器预测活动发生的位置以及每个活跃位置上出现的模式。我们在涵盖人类脑类器官和急性离体人类海马组织的31个实验上对该模型进行了评估。学习到的模式被广泛复用：一个……
tldr: 该论文提出了一种基于共享时空模式词表的离散生成模型，通过残差向量量化自编码器和分解式掩码变换器，解决了高密度微电极阵列中神经元尖峰数据稀疏且电极子集在不同实验间变化的问题，并在人类脑类器官和离体海马组织数据上验证了其有效性。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces a discrete generative model that represents sparse, variable-electrode neuronal spiking activity on high-density microelectrode arrays using a shared vocabulary of spatiotemporal motifs, learned via a residual vector-quantized autoencoder and a factorized masked transformer, validated on 31 assays spanning human brain organoids and acute ex vivo human hippocampal tissue.
